mainPoints.explanation: At 38, he equaled Miroslav Klose's all-time World Cup goal record and delivered a vintage performance against Algeria.
mainPoints.point: Messi's hat-trick on his 200th Argentina appearance proved his enduring quality.

mainPoints.explanation: To prove himself on merit, Messi followed a tailored training plan beyond club commitments, focusing on peak physical condition.
mainPoints.point: Messi's preparation was unusually rigorous, including double sessions with De Paul.

mainPoints.explanation: The 'Super Liga' small-sided tournament saw Messi score over 80 goals, far exceeding teammates, and his form carried into MLS regular season.
mainPoints.point: Inter Miami's internal competition helped maintain his sharpness before the World Cup.

mainPoints.explanation: The AFA uses data tracking for injury prevention and nutrition, and Physio Walter Insaurralde works with Messi in Miami to fine-tune his body.
mainPoints.point: Argentina's setup—from coaching to AI-driven monitoring—supports Messi's longevity.

mainPoints.explanation: Quotes from Scaloni, Xavi, and Haaland emphasize his relentless will to compete and adapt, even after winning the 2022 World Cup.
mainPoints.point: Messi's competitive drive, not just talent, explains his continued excellence.

oneSentenceSummary: This article examines Lionel Messi's remarkable form at age 38 during the 2026 World Cup, analyzing his preparation, fitness, and enduring brilliance through interviews and behind-the-scenes details.
originalTitle: Lionel Messi — improbably， still as good as ever
summary: A deep-dive analysis of Lionel Messi's performance and preparation for the 2026 World Cup, where he scored a hat-trick against Algeria in Argentina's opener. The piece traces his journey from uncertainty about participating, through a demanding training regimen with Argentina teammate Rodrigo De Paul and Inter Miami's internal 'Super Liga' competition, to his injury scare and rapid recovery. Featuring quotes from Scaloni, Xavi, Haaland, and anonymous sources, it explores Messi's diet, fitness adaptation to MLS, and the family-like atmosphere of the Argentina camp. The article argues that Messi, improbably, remains as good as ever, driven by competitiveness and meticulous physical preparation.
title: Lionel Messi — improbably， still as good as ever
